## Summary

I wired up queue and mail infrastructure (neither existed in this app before) and used it to send a welcome email on registration without blocking the response:

- **`config/queue.ts`** / **`config/mail.ts`** — new config files that pick a driver/transport from `QUEUE_CONNECTION` (`sync` default, `redis` via `REDIS_URL`, `memory` for tests) and `MAIL_MAILER` (`log` default, `resend` via `RESEND_API_KEY`, `memory` for tests), with `from` sourced from `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`/`MAIL_FROM_NAME`.
- **`app/Providers/QueueProvider.ts`** / **`app/Providers/MailProvider.ts`** — bind `QueueManager`/`MailManager` singletons and, in `boot()`, register the welcome-email job and set the framework's global queue driver / mail manager (`Job.dispatch()` and queued-job handlers resolve through those globals, independent of any request's container — this is also what lets a test swap in a holding queue/recording transport after boot).
- **`app/Jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts`** — a `Job` whose `handle()` builds and sends the email (subject `Welcome to ${APP_NAME}, ${name}!`, plain-text greeting, default sender from mail config) via `getMailManager()`.
- **`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.ts`** — after creating the user (and only then, so a refused registration dispatches nothing), calls `SendWelcomeEmailJob.dispatch({ email, name })`; login/redirect to `/dashboard` is unchanged.
- **`src/app.ts`** — registers `MailProvider`/`QueueProvider`.
- **`tests/RegisterController.test.ts`** — new test that points the queue at `MemoryDriver` and mail at a `MemoryTransport`, registers a user, asserts one job is queued and nothing sent yet, runs it via `processJob`, and asserts exactly one correctly-addressed email; a second test confirms a rejected registration (invalid email) queues and sends nothing.

`bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (4/4).
